```plato

//==
// # Algebraic operation interfaces
//
// The elementary arithmetic capabilities, each one small algebraic structure:
// addition, multiplication, division, remainder, inversion, scalar scaling, and
// linear blending. Numeric, vector, and quantity types assemble them as needed.

// An additive group: addition, subtraction, negation, and the identity element
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Additive_group). Zero lives here rather than on
// INumericalLimits because it is an algebraic property of the group, not a fact
// about representation: a IQuantity or a IMatrix is an additive group without
// being a number, and a `where T: IAdditive` bound must be able to name the
// identity for any fold or accumulation seeded from it.
interface IAdditive
{
    Add(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
    Subtract(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
    Negative(x: Self): Self;
    Zero(x: Self): Self;
}

// A multiplicative operation between two values of the same type. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplication)
interface IMultiplicative
{
    Multiply(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
}

// Division between two values of the same type. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Division_(mathematics))
interface IDivisible
{
    Divide(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
}

// Remainder arithmetic between two values of the same type. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modulo_operation)
interface IModular
{
    Modulo(a: Self, b: Self): Self;
}

// Has a multiplicative inverse (reciprocal). (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplicative_inverse)
interface IInvertible
{
    Inverse(x: Self): Self;
}

// The four basic operations plus remainder: a field with modulo. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_(mathematics))
interface IArithmetic
    inherits IAdditive, IMultiplicative, IDivisible, IModular
{ }

// Can be multiplied and divided by a unitless scalar (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scalar_multiplication).
// Vectors, quantities, and colors are scalable even when they cannot multiply
// among themselves.
interface IScalable
{
    Multiply(x: Self, scalar: Number): Self;
    Divide(x: Self, scalar: Number): Self;
    Modulo(x: Self, scalar: Number): Self;
}

// Supports linear interpolation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_interpolation).
// The parameter t is unclamped: 0 yields a, 1 yields b, values outside [0,1]
// extrapolate.
interface IInterpolatable
{
    Lerp(a: Self, b: Self, t: Number): Self;
}
```
